correctness.rationale: The orthogonal real three-tone basis has positive exact norms A,B at every d>0; its squared point-evaluation norm is the sum of reciprocally weighted squared basis values. Direct entire-series division yields the displayed order-q^2 identity with P,Q. P is negative through y=1/2 and strictly increasing for y>=1/2, with unique zero. Q modulo P equals -4R/5 with R positive at that zero, so the critical quartic term is negative. The analytic implicit-function theorem yields the single emerging positive stationary gap, its strict local maximality and sharp square-root onset; direct algebra gives the gain coefficient. The packaged checker verifies eight rational Taylor triples and 96 independent Gram inversions. Finite checks supplement, not replace, the proof.
